## Claims
- [source-backed] The 2011 paper defines \(i=s-t+1,\ j=r-t+1\), identifies \(J_{v_{r,s,t,n}}\subset\Lambda/I_{r,n-r}\), and proves its two integral generating families, with \(a=\min(n-r-i,r-j)\), \(b=\min(i,j)\). [arxiv:0809.2981v2, lines 847-892]
- [source-backed] The same paper labels minimality of those two families as Conjecture 4.10, verified there only for \(r\le4\) and \(n-r\le5\). [arxiv:0809.2981v2, lines 938-975]
- [source-backed] Metadata/abstract for St. Dizier–Yong (2024), *Presenting the cohomology of a Schubert variety: Proof of the minimality conjecture*, states: “We prove the minimality conjecture” and mentions the Hopf algebra of symmetric functions. [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832]
- [unsupported] No supplied full-text excerpt for doi:10.1112/jlms.12832 gives its exact theorem statement, hypotheses, coefficient ring, or definitions; therefore its theorem cannot be compared rigorously with the current integral objects \(A=\Lambda/I_{r,n-r}\) and \(J_v\).
- [unsupported] The requested 2024-theorem target is **not established** by the inspected sources. The bounded search found the relevant 2024 paper only at metadata/abstract level, which is insufficient for theorem-level grounding.

## Strategy
Compared the current objects with the full-text 2011 formulation, then inspected the targeted 2024 candidate. The latter has no citable full-text passage in the supplied search record.

## Gaps
Missing: bounded full-text lines from the 2024 paper containing the theorem, its hypotheses, coefficient ring, and definitions of the ideal and proposed families.

## Next
Obtain a bounded full-text excerpt for doi:10.1112/jlms.12832 before asserting that its theorem applies to the current objects.
